title: identity.v1
description: The identity contract: a scoped API token (subject + scopes + expiry, derived from the admin-api APIToken/`/internal/validate` shape) and an access decision (the canAccess verdict over a resource). Auth itself is transport-layer; these are the data shapes the identity core mints, validates, and decides over.

Scope.description: A capability a token carries. Mirrors admin-models VALID_SCOPES: bot (spawn/control bots), tx (read transcripts), browser (browser sessions).

ResourceKind.description: The kind of resource an access decision is made over. The three guarded read paths: a meeting's transcript, a recording, and the WS subscribe / agent read.

Action.description: The action attempted on a resource. Reads are what canAccess guards today; write/admin reserved for additive growth.

ScopedToken.description: A minted, scope-bounded credential. `subject` is the owning user id (admin-api User.id). The DB scopes column is authoritative upstream; here scopes[] is the sealed shape. `expires_at` null = non-expiring.

subject.description: Owning principal — the user id the token authenticates as.

scopes.description: Capabilities granted. Non-empty; each member is a Scope.

expires_at.description: RFC3339 instant after which the token is rejected. null = never expires.

email.description: Optional human identity carried for audit/attribution (admin-api User.email).

WorkspaceGrant.description: One workspace a dispatch may mount, at a mode (the write-access source of truth).

DispatchClaims.description: The verified claims of a per-dispatch SIGNED token — the chain of custody. Minted per dispatch by the Identity service (subject + launcher + workspace/tool grants), attested by the Runtime, verified at every boundary — never by the agent. The wire form is an opaque signed compact token; this is its decoded payload. Authority is re-derived from these claims, not from the (tamperable) request.

sub.description: subject — the principal acted on behalf of

lch.description: launcher — who/what triggered the dispatch (holds a delegation grant)

ws.description: workspace grants the workspace-store boundary enforces

tools.description: tool grants the MCP-gateway boundary enforces

ValidateRequest.description: The body of POST /internal/validate, the authz oracle the gateway, flows and the terminal's server call on the internal tier (X-Internal-Secret = INTERNAL_API_SECRET). `token` is an API key or a worker's delegation token (delegation.v1, prefix `vxd_`). Failures: 503 when INTERNAL_API_SECRET is unset outside dev mode, and 503 `Delegation revocation store unavailable` for a delegation token whose revocation (delegation.v1 jti, revoked when its unit ends) cannot be checked, which never applies to an API key; 403 on a wrong internal secret; 401 with detail `Missing token`, `Invalid token`, `Token expired`, `Delegation tokens are not accepted on this deployment` (no VEXA_MCP_DELEGATION_SECRET), `Invalid delegation: <delegation.v1 RefusalReason>`, `Invalid delegation: scope` (a verified token whose `scope` is not a delegation.v1 Scope) or `Invalid delegation: no such user`. A delegation token is answered only to a caller that sends AcceptsDelegationHeader; to any other caller it is `Invalid token`.

AcceptsDelegationHeader.description: The request header a caller of POST /internal/validate sends, with the value `1`, to declare that it reads `delegation` and `person_is_admin` and enforces the ceiling. Identity answers a delegation token (`vxd_`) 200 ONLY to a caller that sends it; to any other caller the token is refused exactly like a bearer nobody answers to (401 `Invalid token`), so a resolver that predates delegation fails closed instead of taking a worker for its person. A value other than `1` is no declaration. An API key is answered the same with or without it. Callers that send it: the gateway (from v0.13.2) and flows-api. The header is in the x-vexa-internal- family, which the gateway never forwards from a client. Header names are case-insensitive.

ValidateDelegation.description: The ceiling a delegation token's dispatch was granted (delegation.v1 `scope`, plus its `target`), passed on for the services behind the gateway to enforce. It becomes gateway-identity.v1 `delegation`.

ValidateResponse.description: The 200 answer of POST /internal/validate: who the bearer is. For an API key, `scopes` are the key's (`legacy` for a key minted before scopes) and `is_admin` is identity's admin test for its owner. For a delegation token, `scopes` are exactly [bot, tx], `is_admin` is always false (a worker is never the admin), `delegation` carries the dispatch's ceiling and `person_is_admin` says whether the person it acts for is the instance admin; the gateway treats a worker as the admin only when that is true AND the regime is human. `delegation` and `person_is_admin` appear together and only for a delegation token.

workspaces.description: shared-workspace memberships; for a delegation token, only the person's memberships inside the dispatch's ceiling (delegation.v1 ceiling_reads)

AccessDecision.description: The verdict canAccess(subject, resource, action) returns. Default-deny: `allow=false` unless a policy explicitly grants. `reason` is a stable machine code, not free text.
